newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to audit firms controlled by govt.
newsitem.headline: Russia to audit firms controlled by govt.

text.p: The Russian government will audit companies where it has a controlling stake in 1997, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.

Igor Shabdurasulov told a news conference the list of companies to be audited included gas monopoly RAO Gazprom GAZP.RTS, national power company UES EESR.RTS, NK Rosneft oil group, insurer Rosgosstrakh and Aeroflot International Airlines.
Other organisations on the list are AO Rosugol coal company, AO Transneft oil pipe company, Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport, AO Sovkomflot trade vessel company and the Railway Ministry.

"The aim of the check is to recommend to the government as the major or sole shareholder what to do next with its property," a Russian Privatisation Centre official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
The Russian Privatisation Centre carried out a tender for choosing audit companies.

The official said the audit would mean a check of whether expenses were included in production costs correctly, whether budget money was spent for what has been provided and whether price policies were correct.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is funding the project, he said.
He said the audit firms were chosen at a tender according to EBRD criteria, but refused to name them. Major Russian firms and two big Western firms were chosen.
He said the firms chosen by the government were not the same as those chosen by the companies themselves for their audits.
He said the audit would not start before the end of May and was likely to last longer than the officially stipulated 10 weeks.
The State Property Committee will supervise the audits, a government regulation obtained by Reuters says.
